subject: Chemistry
title: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
summary: Alcohols (R–OH) and phenols (Ar–OH) have an –OH group; ethers (R–O–R′) have oxygen between two carbons. Hydrogen bonding gives alcohols and phenols high boiling points and some water solubility.
Phenols are much more acidic than alcohols because the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised; electron-withdrawing groups (–NO₂) at ortho/para make phenol even more acidic.
Alcohols react by breaking O–H (acidity, esterification) or C–O (substitution, dehydration). The Lucas test distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.

The –OH group strongly activates the benzene ring of phenol towards electrophilic substitution (bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol). Named reactions: Kolbe, Reimer–Tiemann, Williamson synthesis.

formulas.name: Alcohols from alkenes
formulas.formula: acid-catalysed hydration (Markovnikov);  hydroboration–oxidation (B₂H₆ then H₂O₂/OH⁻) gives anti-Markovnikov alcohols

formulas.name: Alcohols from carbonyls
formulas.formula: RCHO + H₂/Ni or NaBH₄/LiAlH₄ → 1° alcohol;  R₂CO → 2° alcohol;  RCOOH + LiAlH₄ → 1° alcohol

formulas.name: Grignard route
formulas.formula: HCHO + RMgX → 1° alcohol;  other aldehydes → 2°;  ketones → 3° (after hydrolysis)
formulas.when: Building alcohols with new C–C bonds.

formulas.name: Acidity order
formulas.note: Electron-donating groups (–CH₃) decrease phenol's acidity; electron-withdrawing groups (–NO₂) increase it.

formulas.name: Lucas test
formulas.formula: conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl₂:  3° turbidity immediately;  2° within ~5 min;  1° only on heating

formulas.name: Dehydration of alcohols
formulas.formula: conc. H₂SO₄ heat: ethanol → ethene (443 K) or diethyl ether (413 K);  ease 3° > 2° > 1°
formulas.note: Temperature decides the product: higher gives the alkene, lower gives the ether.

formulas.name: Oxidation of alcohols
formulas.formula: 1° → aldehyde (PCC) → acid (KMnO₄);  2° → ketone;  3° resist oxidation;  Cu at 573 K: 1° → aldehyde, 2° → ketone, 3° → alkene
formulas.when: Identifying the alcohol type from products.

formulas.name: Phenol preparation
formulas.formula: cumene process (cumene → cumene hydroperoxide → phenol + acetone);  from diazonium salts (warm water);  from chlorobenzene (Dow's process)

formulas.name: Kolbe's reaction
formulas.formula: sodium phenoxide + CO₂ (4–7 atm, 400 K), then H⁺ → salicylic acid

formulas.name: Reimer–Tiemann reaction
formulas.formula: phenol + CHCl₃ + aq. NaOH, then H⁺ → salicylaldehyde

formulas.name: Bromination of phenol
formulas.formula: bromine water → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white ppt);  Br₂ in CS₂ (low temperature) → o- and p-bromophenol

formulas.name: Williamson synthesis
formulas.note: Use a 1° alkyl halide — with 3° halides elimination (alkene) dominates.

formulas.name: Cleavage of ethers by HI
formulas.formula: R–O–CH₃ + HI → R–OH + CH₃I (I⁻ attacks the less hindered carbon);  anisole + HI → phenol + CH₃I
formulas.mistake: The aryl–O bond never breaks: anisole gives phenol, not iodobenzene.

examples.title: Grignard synthesis
examples.problem: Which carbonyl compound and Grignard reagent give 2-methylpropan-2-ol?
examples.solution: Acetone + CH₃MgBr, then hydrolysis → (CH₃)₃COH (a ketone gives a 3° alcohol).

examples.title: Acidity
examples.solution: p-Nitrophenol > phenol > p-cresol > ethanol (–NO₂ stabilises phenoxide; –CH₃ destabilises it; ethoxide has no resonance).

examples.title: Lucas test
examples.problem: Three alcohols give turbidity: one at once, one after 5 minutes, one only on heating. Identify their types.
examples.solution: Immediate: tertiary (2-methylpropan-2-ol); about 5 min: secondary (butan-2-ol); on heating: primary (butan-1-ol).

examples.title: Steam volatility
examples.problem: Why is o-nitrophenol steam volatile but p-nitrophenol not?
examples.solution: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so its molecules don't associate. p-Nitrophenol forms intermolecular H-bonds, which raise its boiling point.

examples.title: Ether cleavage
examples.solution: Phenol + methyl iodide. The O–aryl bond has partial double-bond character, so I⁻ attacks the methyl carbon.

examples.title: Williamson choice
examples.problem: To make tert-butyl methyl ether, which pair: (CH₃)₃CBr + CH₃ONa or CH₃Br + (CH₃)₃CONa?
examples.solution: CH₃Br + (CH₃)₃CONa. A 3° halide with a strong base would undergo elimination to isobutylene.

topics.title: Classification and structure
topics.explain: Alcohols: monohydric, dihydric, trihydric; primary, secondary, tertiary; allylic and benzylic. In alcohols O is sp³ with the C–O–H angle slightly less than tetrahedral; in phenols the C–O bond is shorter (partial double-bond character).

topics.title: Physical properties
topics.explain: Boiling points of alcohols are much higher than those of hydrocarbons and ethers of similar mass (hydrogen bonding); they fall with branching. Lower alcohols mix with water; solubility falls as the alkyl part grows.

topics.title: Reactions of the O–H bond
topics.explain: Alcohols react with active metals (Na) to give H₂ and alkoxides, and with acids, anhydrides or acid chlorides to form esters (esterification). Phenol also reacts with NaOH (alcohols don't), showing its acidic nature is stronger.

topics.title: Electrophilic substitution of phenol
topics.explain: –OH activates the ring at ortho/para. Nitration with dilute HNO₃ gives o- and p-nitrophenol; concentrated HNO₃ gives picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol). Sulphonation with conc. H₂SO₄ gives o-phenolsulphonic acid at low temperature and the p-isomer at higher temperature. Oxidation with chromic acid gives benzoquinone.

topics.title: Mechanism of dehydration
topics.explain: Protonation of –OH, loss of water to form a carbocation (slow step), then loss of H⁺ to form the alkene. Because a carbocation forms, the ease is tertiary > secondary > primary and rearrangements can occur.

topics.title: Commercially important alcohols
topics.explain: Methanol (wood spirit) is poisonous: it causes blindness and death. Ethanol is made by fermentation of sugars (invertase, zymase); denatured alcohol is made unfit to drink with CuSO₄ and pyridine.

topics.title: Ethers
topics.explain: Prepared by Williamson synthesis or dehydration of alcohols. Less polar, with lower boiling points than isomeric alcohols. –OR activates the ring in anisole (o/p-directing) for halogenation, nitration and Friedel–Crafts reactions.

ratta: Ethanol + H₂SO₄: 443 K ethene, 413 K ether.
Williamson: 1° halide + alkoxide;  anisole + HI → phenol + CH₃I.
